answer.open_decision: Whether the command may append a copy of a row that the registry already has, when a starter entry has the id of that row.
answer.reason: Every law that limits new rows skips a row that is already in the registry (x not in r). The starter id order law allows the id 1 once. So a design can append one exact copy of an existing row and still pass all laws.

answer.reason: For a legal input, the laws fix the old registry as a prefix and the new rows as exactly one row per absent starter (AddsOnlyAbsent, AddsAllAbsent, and NoDuplicateOfExisting rule out extras and rows equal to old ones). Distinct ids plus NewInStarterOrder fix their order, copied id, adapter and model fix the identity, and the three enabled laws fix the flag in every case of enable and lock.

For a legal starter list, the laws fix the new rows: the prefix is r, new ids are a sublist of starter ids (no duplicates), each absent starter must give exactly one row, rows of non-absent starters are barred, adapter and model come from the starter, and enabled is fixed in all three cases (enable off, locked, enable on and unlocked).
